reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) shows that trace O/N promote phase segregation and softening during static thermal aging at 700°C, but it does not address segregation under mechanical loading, nucleation of brittle phases at grain boundaries, or a direct link to reduced toughness and brittle fracture. The hypothesis extends the static aging findings to a dynamic, stress-driven mechanism without supporting evidence for the key premises.
premises: Trace interstitials (O, N) segregate under mechanical loading and service conditions
Segregation catalyzes local phase separation into brittle secondary phases
Brittle phases nucleate at grain boundaries or intra-granular regions
Brittle phases reduce plastic deformation, causing toughness loss and brittle fracture
Impurity-doped samples will show lower toughness and brittle features vs. high-purity baseline
